result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days, defaulting to 30. The full test suite passes (`mvn -q -o test`).

- **`model/Supplier.java`**: the record has a new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor still works and gives the standard 30 days, so existing callers and tests didn't need changes.
- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier.payment_terms_days` is a new column, `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, and it can't be negative.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` store the terms, so they can be entered at registration and changed later. All the listings now read the terms: by name, by country, by minimum rating and `findSupplierById`. I also updated the other queries that build a `Supplier` (purchase suggestions, supplier performance and spending, and the category single-supplier report), so they don't silently show 30 for everyone.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: a new test covers the default of 30, a supplier registered at 45 days and renegotiated to 14, and that 14 shows in all four views.

The schema is created fresh each time (in-memory H2), so there is no migration.

I didn't commit.
